value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Client: Employment status, Label' in the Client (DEX Curated) distribution; DSS Data Exchange Protocols version 13, section 7.7
variable_description: What the client said they were doing for work when the record was created or last edited. DSS defines the element as "the employment status of a given client, whether employed or another role, represented by a label", and the label set mixes labour force states with unpaid roles: paid work full-time, paid work part-time, unpaid work including volunteering, unemployed and looking, not working and not looking, studying full-time, studying part-time, caring, and parenting. It is optional partnership-approach data, so it is present only for organisations that opted in and for clients who were asked.
value_definition: A short uppercase label rather than a numeric code, formatted A(6)[A(10)] in the DSS registry. The protocols state the categories are "adapted from the data collection definitions used by Disability Employment Services", not from the ABS labour force framework.
limitation: One label has to carry a person who does several things at once, and the protocols say so directly: a client's employment status can also include being a carer. A working parent, a studying carer and a part-time worker looking for more hours all resolve to a single value chosen by whoever entered the record. Because the categories come from Disability Employment Services rather than the ABS, the values cannot be aligned with a Labour Force Survey or Census employment status without a mapping that DSS does not publish.
rationale: The DSS metadata registry publishes the element definition and its format for the same column name in the curated Data Exchange client table, and the protocols publish the category list and its provenance.
evidence_quote: The employment status of a given client, whether employed or another role, represented by a label.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DSS wording as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing warned that a single label has to absorb caring, parenting and study.

value_domain: ABS Commonwealth Electoral Division code, 2022 boundaries
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Non ABS Structures: Commonwealth Electoral Divisions
variable_description: The federal electorate an address falls in on the 2022 boundaries, assigned by the DSS address validation and geocoder rather than reported by anyone. The column appears on two tables and means two different things: on special_client it is the client's residential address, and on special_outlet it is the service outlet's address, where the DIL's own label still reads 'Client Address' and is wrong. ABS defines these divisions as "an ABS Mesh Block approximation of Australian Electoral Commission (AEC) federal electoral divisions", so the code is a statistical rendering of the electorate, not the AEC's legal boundary.
value_definition: A three-digit code: one digit for state or territory and two digits for the division, numbered alphabetically within each state. The 2022 vintage is fixed, so the code reflects the AEC boundaries in force for that year and not any later redistribution.
limitation: An electorate changes under the feet of a person who never moves. The AEC redistributes divisions between elections, so this column cannot be compared with a division from another vintage, and a client appearing in a different electorate across two extracts has usually been re-coded rather than relocated. On the client table the underlying address is also unreliable for the people most likely to be studied: the protocols allow a homeless client to be recorded at the outlet's suburb and postcode, which puts them in the service's electorate.
rationale: The ABS publishes the definition, the coding structure and the AEC-approximation basis of Commonwealth Electoral Divisions in the ASGS non-ABS structures. The PLIDA registry shows the column on both the client and outlet tables with a geocoder-assigned description.
evidence_quote: Commonwealth Electoral Divisions are an ABS Mesh Block approximation of Australian Electoral Commission (AEC) federal electoral divisions.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the DIL's 'Client Address: 2022 Federal Electorate Boundary Code' on both tables, which is wrong on the outlet table, and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice.

value_domain: ABS Standard for Sex, Gender, Variations of Sex Characteristics and Sexual Orientation Variables gender category
value_source: DSS Data Exchange Protocols version 13, section 6.1.3; ABS Standard for Sex, Gender, Variations of Sex Characteristics and Sexual Orientation Variables
variable_description: The client's self-identified gender, and one of the four inputs to the linkage key that makes this dataset joinable at all. The protocols state that "a client's gender is recorded because it forms part of the SLK and is recorded based upon how the client self-identifies", and that the Data Exchange uses the ABS standard with five options: man or male, woman or female, non-binary, a different term, and prefer not to answer. This is a mandatory field, unlike most of the client attributes beside it.
value_definition: A short label of up to eight characters in the DSS registry, drawn from the ABS gender standard rather than from a sex classification. ABS treats gender as "a social and cultural concept" about identity and experience, and consolidates free-text 'different term' responses with non-binary in published output.
limitation: Because gender feeds the statistical linkage key alongside name letters and date of birth, a client recorded as one gender at one organisation and another at a second generates two keys and appears in the data as two people. That makes the field a linkage risk as much as a demographic variable, and it makes a change of recorded gender over time indistinguishable from a data entry correction. The field is also not sex and cannot be used where a biological measure is wanted.
rationale: The Data Exchange Protocols state the collection rule, the ABS standard it follows and the five response options, and the same document sets out the linkage key algorithm that consumes the field.
evidence_quote: A client's gender is recorded because it forms part of the SLK and is recorded based upon how the client self-identifies.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried a garbled DIL sentence about male, female and 'other genders which are a combination of male and female' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, when the protocols publish the five options and their source.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Client: Has a carer, Flag' in the Client (DEX Curated) distribution; DSS Data Exchange Protocols version 13, section 6.3.1
variable_description: Whether somebody is caring for this client, which is the mirror image of ISCARER on the same row. DSS defines it as "whether a given client is the care recipient in a carer relationship, represented by a flag", and the protocols set it as a mandatory yes-or-no question for Commonwealth Home Support Programme activities, where it exists "to determine how many clients have care arrangements in place". Outside that programme it is rarely populated.
value_definition: A boolean flag, held as a single digit in the DSS registry. The carer concept behind it is the protocols' own: a person providing unpaid care and support to family or friends with a disability, mental illness, chronic or terminal condition, an alcohol or other drug issue, or who are frail aged.
limitation: The carer is not a person in this data. There is no carer identifier, no carer record and no link, so a care recipient cannot be paired with their carer even when both are Data Exchange clients and both have a row on special_client. Because the question is mandatory only for one programme, a blank almost always means the client was never asked rather than that nobody cares for them.
rationale: The DSS metadata registry publishes the element definition for the same column name in the curated client table, and the protocols state where the question is mandatory and what it is for.
evidence_quote: Whether a given client is the care recipient in a carer relationship, represented by a flag.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DSS wording as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without saying that the carer is not represented anywhere in the data.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Client: Homelessness status, Label' in the Client (DEX Curated) distribution; DSS Data Exchange Protocols version 13, section 7.10
variable_description: Whether the client said they were homeless, at risk of homelessness, or neither. DSS defines the element as "the experience of unstable, inadequate or non-permanent housing identified by a given client, represented by a label", and the protocols set the three values as Yes, No and At Risk: a person is homeless if they have no suitable accommodation alternative and their current arrangement is in an inadequate dwelling, has no tenure or only short and non-extendable tenure, or does not allow control of and access to space for social relations. At risk covers major structural problems, constant threat of violence, crowding, improvised dwellings and marginal housing such as caravan parks.
value_definition: A short label of up to six characters in the DSS registry, holding one of three states rather than a yes-no flag. The three-part scale follows the ABS statistical definition of homelessness rather than a service eligibility test.
limitation: The value belongs to the client record, not to any session, so it is the answer as at the version of the client row you are reading. The row is versioned by SYSSTARTTIME, SYSENDTIME, RECORDSEQNBR and CURRENTRECORD, and joining the current version to an old session backdates a housing status that may have been recorded years later. The protocols also say the answer "should be based solely on what is reported by the client", so a service's own assessment never overrides it and a client who does not describe themselves as homeless is recorded as not homeless.
rationale: The DSS metadata registry publishes the element definition and format for the same column name in the curated client table, and the protocols publish the three values and the homelessness definition behind them.
evidence_quote: The experience of unstable, inadequate or non-permanent housing identified by a given client, represented by a label.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DSS wording as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, when the protocols publish the three values, the definition and the self-report rule.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Client: Household composition, Label' in the Client (DEX Curated) distribution; DSS Data Exchange Protocols version 13, section 7.5
variable_description: Who the client lives with, in one of eight categories: living alone, sole parent with dependants, couple, couple with dependants, group of related adults, group of unrelated adults, homeless or no household, and not stated. The protocols state the categories are "adapted from the data collection definitions used by AIHW" and that the classification "is adapted to include data on whether the client is homeless". It is optional partnership-approach data, so absence is common and is not a household type.
value_definition: A label of up to ten characters in the DSS registry, formatted AAAAA[XAAAA]. Seven of the eight categories describe a living arrangement; the eighth records that there is no household to describe.
limitation: The other members of the household are not identified. There is no household key, no link between client records and no way to find a partner or a child who is also a Data Exchange client, so this column cannot be used to build households or to attribute a service to a family. The homeless category also makes the field two variables in one: a client coded Homeless/No household has an unknown living arrangement rather than a recorded one, so dropping that category from a distribution silently drops the most disadvantaged clients.
rationale: The DSS metadata registry publishes the element definition and format for the same column name in the curated client table, and the protocols publish the eight categories and state the AIHW basis and the homelessness adaptation.
evidence_quote: Household composition is classified into standard categories that are adapted from the data collection definitions used by AIHW. Household composition is adapted to include data on whether the client is homeless.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DSS wording 'Describes the client's living arrangements, represented by a label' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, when the protocols publish the eight categories.

value_domain: Self-reported gross income in whole Australian dollars
value_source: DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), section 7.8.2
variable_description: How much the client said they earn, before tax, over whatever period INCOMEFREQUENCYCODE names. The protocols state that the field is "a numerical value for the estimated dollar amount of the client's gross income (earnings before tax)", that it "is based on what is reported by the client and no evidence of income is required", and that income frequency must be recorded for an amount to be recorded at all. It is optional partnership-approach data.
value_definition: A whole-dollar number with no period attached to it. The web portal accepts the amount as a weekly, fortnightly, monthly or annual figure, so the number is uninterpretable on its own and has to be annualised against INCOMEFREQUENCYCODE before any two clients can be compared.
limitation: This is one person's estimate of their own income, not a measured or verified amount, and it is the client's income rather than the household's, so it cannot be used to place a client against a household income threshold or a poverty line. It is also a snapshot on a client record that changes only when someone edits it, so it is not a time series and cannot show an income change over a spell of service.
rationale: The Data Exchange Protocols set out the units, the gross basis, the self-report rule, the absence of verification and the dependency on income frequency for this exact field.
evidence_quote: Data is recorded as a numerical value for the estimated dollar amount of the client's gross income (earnings before tax). This is based on what is reported by the client and no evidence of income is required.
supersedes_rationale: The entry guessed a monetary domain from the variable name, described it as 'Descibes the amount of income that a given client receives', and gave a boilerplate limitation about inferred domains rather than warning that the figure is meaningless without the frequency.

value_source: DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), section 7.8.2
variable_description: The period the dollar figure in INCOMEAMOUNT refers to: weekly, fortnightly, monthly or annually. It exists because the Data Exchange lets clients answer in whatever period they think in, and the protocols make it compulsory whenever an amount is given, stating that "income frequency must be recorded in order to be able to record the approximate gross income". Without it the amount beside it cannot be read.
value_definition: One of four period labels. The scale is not ordinal and carries no dollar information of its own; its only job is to supply the denominator for the amount on the same row.
limitation: The frequency is how the client chose to quote a figure, not how often they are actually paid, so it says nothing about pay cycle, casual work or the regularity of income. A client paid weekly who answers with an annual estimate is recorded as annual. It is also no help where the amount is missing: a frequency on its own conveys nothing.
rationale: The Data Exchange Protocols name the four frequencies in the list of data values and state the rule that binds this field to the income amount.
evidence_quote: Income frequency must be recorded in order to be able to record the approximate gross income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL wording 'Describes the frequency of income that a given client receives' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, when the four values are published and the field's whole purpose is to make the amount readable.

value_domain: Data Exchange main source of income label
value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Client: Main source of income, Code' in the Client (DEX Curated) distribution; DSS Data Exchange Protocols version 13, section 7.8.1
variable_description: Where most of the client's money comes from, in one of six categories: nil income, employee salary or wages, self-employment from an unincorporated business, government payments, pensions and allowances, other income including superannuation and investments, and not stated. DSS defines it as "the main source of income for a given client, represented by a label", and the protocols state the categories are "based on the data collection definitions used by the AIHW". value_definition: A label of up to twelve characters in the DSS registry, formatted AAA[A(9)]. It names the largest single source only, not a composition, so it cannot be split or apportioned.
