A client on a part-rate payment topping up part-time wages appears under one heading, so the column cannot measure reliance on income support or count people with any earned income. It is also the client's own account and is not reconciled with the payments data: someone coded to government payments here may have no DOMINO record, and someone coded to wages may be receiving a payment.
rationale: The DSS metadata registry publishes the element definition and format for the same column name in the curated client table, and the protocols publish the six categories and their AIHW basis.
evidence_quote: The main source of income for a given client, represented by a label.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DSS wording as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, when the six categories are published and the main-source restriction is the field's central weakness.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Client: Is a carer, Flag' in the Client (DEX Curated) distribution; DSS Data Exchange Protocols version 13, section 7.12
variable_description: Whether the client says they care for somebody, which is the mirror image of HASCARER on the same row. DSS defines it as "whether a given client is a carer in a carer relationship, represented by a flag", and the protocols define a carer as "a person who provides unpaid care and support to family members and friends who have a disability, mental illness, chronic condition, terminal illness, an alcohol or other drug issue or who are frail aged". It is optional partnership-approach data recorded as yes or no.
value_definition: A boolean flag, held as a single digit in the DSS registry. The protocols state the field is "based on the client's reported caring situation", so it records identification rather than an assessment of caring hours or intensity.
limitation: Self-identification undercounts caring badly, because much of the care that meets the DSS definition is provided by people who describe themselves as a spouse, a parent or a daughter rather than a carer. The flag is also blank far more often than it is false, since it is optional, so treating a missing value as no inflates the non-carer group. Anyone counted here as a carer may separately appear with EMPLOYMENTSTATUSCODE of caring, and the two are collected under different rules.
rationale: The DSS metadata registry publishes the element definition and format for the same column name in the curated client table, and the protocols publish the carer definition and the self-report rule.
evidence_quote: A carer is defined as a person who provides unpaid care and support to family members and friends who have a disability, mental illness, chronic condition, terminal illness, an alcohol or other drug issue or who are frail aged.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DSS wording as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, with nothing about the definition behind the flag or its known undercount.

value_source: DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), sections 5.4 and 6.1.1
variable_description: Marks a client record built on a made-up name, and so a record that will not link. The protocols tell organisations that "where a client does not wish to disclose their real name, the organisation should indicate that a pseudonym is being used and record a pseudonym that ideally is used again if the client returns for other services". It matters far beyond privacy because the statistical linkage key is built from letters of the family and given name together with date of birth and gender, so a pseudonym changes the key.
value_definition: A tick box in the web portal, carried into the data as a flag. It records that a pseudonym was used, not what the pseudonym was and not why.
limitation: The flag warns that a record is unlinkable but does nothing to repair it. A pseudonymous client's key is derived from a false name, so their service history will not join to their real records elsewhere in the Data Exchange or to any linked collection, and a client who used different pseudonyms at two organisations appears as two different people with no way to detect it. Pseudonym use is concentrated in refuge and family violence services, so the linkage loss is not random and falls on the clients most likely to be of interest.
rationale: The Data Exchange Protocols publish the pseudonym instruction, list the field as a tick box in the client data values, and set out the linkage key algorithm that consumes the client's name.
evidence_quote: Where a client does not wish to disclose their 'real' name, the organisation should indicate that a pseudonym is being used and record a pseudonym that ideally is used again if the client returns for other services.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Pseudonym used flag. Indicates clients who use pseudonym instead of their real name' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without saying that the flag marks a broken linkage key.

value_domain: ABS Local Government Area code, 2016 boundaries
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Non ABS Structures: Local Government Areas
variable_description: The council area an address falls in on the 2016 boundaries, assigned by the DSS address validation and geocoder. It appears on two tables with two meanings: on special_client it is the client's residential address and on special_outlet it is the outlet's, where the DIL's 'Client Address' label is a copy that was never corrected. ABS defines these areas as "an ABS Mesh Block approximation of gazetted local government boundaries as defined by each state and territory", and pairs on the same row with SA12016, SA22016, SA32016, SA42016 and STE2016, all cut from the same 2016 vintage.
value_definition: A five-digit code: one digit for state or territory and four for the area, always ending in zero. Parts of Australia that no incorporated council administers are carried as ordinary areas named Unincorporated followed by the state or territory. Separate non-spatial special purpose codes sit outside the legally designated areas as balancing items, for people coded to migratory, offshore and shipping mesh blocks, to no usual address, and to outside Australia.
limitation: The code is a statistical approximation and not the legal council boundary, so it must never be used to decide which council an address is rated by, which by-laws apply, or who is entitled to a council service. Parts of Australia have no incorporated council at all and still carry an ordinary code rather than a missing value, so an unincorporated area enters a distribution looking like a council.
rationale: The ABS publishes the definition, the five-digit coding structure and the special purpose codes for Local Government Areas in the ASGS non-ABS structures. The PLIDA registry shows the column on both the client and outlet tables with a geocoder-assigned description.
evidence_quote: Local Government Areas are an ABS Mesh Block approximation of gazetted local government boundaries as defined by each state and territory.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the DIL's 'Client Address: 2016 Local Government Area Boundary Code' on both tables, which is wrong on the outlet table, and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice.

value_domain: ABS Local Government Area code, 2021 boundaries
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Non ABS Structures: Local Government Areas
variable_description: The same address placed on the 2021 council boundaries, sitting next to the 2016 code rather than replacing it. Both editions are carried on special_client and special_outlet so that a record can be matched to whichever vintage a comparison dataset uses: the 2021 code aligns with the 2021 Census and with ASGS Edition 3 geography, the 2016 code with the 2016 Census. Where the two columns disagree for one row, the address did not move; the boundary did.
value_definition: A five-digit code: one digit for state or territory and four for the area, always ending in zero. There are 567 areas in the current release covering all of Australia, including unincorporated areas and nineteen non-spatial special purpose codes.
limitation: The 2021 and 2016 columns are not a before-and-after measure of anything about the client. Councils amalgamated and split between the editions and codes were reissued, so a series built by switching from one column to the other at 2021 shows a step change that is administrative. Choose one vintage for a whole analysis and match it to the vintage of whatever the geography is being joined to.
rationale: The ABS publishes the definition, coding structure and count of Local Government Areas in the ASGS non-ABS structures. That the two vintages sit side by side on the same PLIDA row, rather than one superseding the other, is read from the registry table structure rather than from a published statement.
evidence_quote: Local Government Areas are an ABS Mesh Block approximation of gazetted local government boundaries as defined by each state and territory.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the DIL's 'Client Address: 2021 Local Government Area Boundary Code' on both tables and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing explained why two vintages of the same geography sit side by side.

value_domain: ABS Australian Standard Classification of Languages 2016, language code
value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Client: Main language spoken at home, ASCL 2016 code' in the Client (DEX Curated) distribution; ABS Australian Standard Classification of Languages, 2016
variable_description: The language the client says is mainly spoken in their home, coded to the ABS classification rather than written out. DSS names the element "Client: Main language spoken at home, ASCL 2016 code" and defines it as "the main language spoken at home by a given client, represented by a code". It is one of two cultural and linguistic diversity items collected as a priority requirement, the other being country of birth, and both are recorded as reported by the client.
value_definition: A four-digit code from the Australian Standard Classification of Languages 2016, which covers 435 languages including 44 'not elsewhere classified' categories. The leading digit is the broad group and the first two digits the narrow group, so the code can be collapsed without a mapping table.
limitation: A language spoken at home is not a statement of English proficiency and not a statement of need for an interpreter. INTERPRETERPRESENT on the session record answers the second question and disagrees with this column often in both directions: a bilingual client who speaks another language at home may need no help, and a client who speaks English at home may attend with a parent who does not. The classification is fixed at the 2016 edition, which is the edition the 2021 Census also used, so the two line up; the ABS released a new edition in 2025, and language data coded on that edition will not join to this column without a correspondence.
rationale: The DSS metadata registry names the classification and edition in the element name for the same column in the curated client table and publishes the four-digit format. The ABS publishes the structure and scope of the 2016 classification.
evidence_quote: The main language spoken at home by a given client, represented by a code.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DSS wording as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without naming the classification the codes come from.

value_source: DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), section 7.13
variable_description: What the service recorded about the client's standing with the National Disability Insurance Scheme, in one of three states: eligible, ineligible, or an access request in progress. The protocols say the field reports "the NDIS eligibility of a client, and if they have an application in progress", which is why a pending application is a value rather than a missing one. It is optional partnership-approach data and is most often populated in disability advocacy and support activities.
value_definition: One of three labels published in the protocols' list of data values. The three states are not ordered and the in-progress value is a process state rather than a degree of eligibility.
limitation: This is the organisation's understanding, not a decision by the National Disability Insurance Agency, so an eligible label here is not an access decision and can be wrong in either direction. The NDIS data in PLIDA carries the actual access request and its outcome, and comparing the two is a check on the service's knowledge rather than a duplicate measure. Because the field is optional, blank is not ineligible.
rationale: The Data Exchange Protocols define the field and list its three values, and state that it is optional partnership-approach data reported by the organisation.
evidence_quote: Data is reported on the NDIS eligibility of a client, and if they have an application in progress. This field is optional.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL wording and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, when the three values are published and the distinction from an NDIA decision is the thing a reader needs.

value_domain: Data Exchange client exit reason label
value_source: DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), section 7.16
variable_description: Why the client's involvement with a case ended, recorded on the attendance row that closed it. The protocols publish nine reasons: needs met, no longer requires assistance, service unable to assist, now requires a higher level of care, moved out of area, client terminated the service, client died, no longer eligible, and none of the above. Two of them turn on cause rather than outcome, and the protocols say so: needs met is for improvement "as a result of the reason they sought assistance and the service they received", while no longer requires assistance covers improvement "not necessarily because the service met their needs".
value_definition: One of nine published labels, unordered. The distinction between the two positive reasons is an attribution judgement made by the organisation, not a measured outcome.
limitation: Most cases carry no exit reason at all, because the field is optional partnership-approach data, so a missing value cannot be read as a case still open. The two positive categories are also not comparable across organisations: whether an improvement is credited to the service is a judgement, and an organisation with an incentive to show results has every reason to prefer needs met. Use the reason to describe how services end, not to measure whether they worked; the paired SCORE ratings are the outcome measure.
rationale: The Data Exchange Protocols publish the nine exit reasons with a definition of each and state the attribution distinction between the two positive categories in their own words.
evidence_quote: This may be used where a client's circumstances have improved to the point that they no longer require assistance, but not necessarily because the service met their needs.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the protocols' introductory sentence as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without listing the reasons or flagging the attribution judgement inside them.

value_domain: Rural Financial Counselling Service external referral destination label
value_source: DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), section 6.3.5 and the list of data values
variable_description: What kind of outside service a rural financial counselling client was sent on to. The protocols define it as an item "used to describe a client's referral to another service from the Rural Financial Counselling Service", and it is the only place in the Data Exchange that records a referral destination rather than a referral purpose. The twelve values are drawn from the world a farm business operates in: health professional, financial institution, legal aid or solicitor, accountant or financial adviser, real estate agent, agronomist, succession planner, social support group, training organisation, other government agency, asset agent, and other. It appears only for Rural Financial Counselling Service program activities and is empty on every other session.
value_definition: One of twelve published labels naming a type of destination, not a named organisation. The list is program specific and does not apply to, or align with, the general referral purpose categories used elsewhere in the Data Exchange.
limitation: A destination type is not evidence the client went. The Data Exchange records the referral as made and never records an arrival, so a count here measures counselling practice rather than client take-up. Because the field exists only for one program, it also cannot be used to compare referral behaviour between programs, and its absence on a session is not the absence of a referral: REFERRALTOEXTERNALKEY on the attendance record carries general external referrals with a purpose but no destination.
rationale: The Data Exchange Protocols define the item under Rural Financial Counselling Service mandatory fields and publish the twelve destination values in the list of data values.
evidence_quote: External Referral Destination: this item is used to describe a client's referral to another service from the Rural Financial Counselling Service.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the protocols' one-line definition and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, when the twelve destinations are published and the program restriction is what governs whether the column is usable.

value_domain: Session fee in whole Australian dollars
value_source: DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), sections 6.3.1 and 6.3.2
variable_description: What the people attending a session were charged to be there. The protocols describe it as a session-level item that "allows organisations to report whether the participants of the session were charged a fee to attend the service and reflects the program activity policy regarding fee collection", captured as a dollar figure. It is a mandatory field only for Commonwealth Home Support Programme and Family Law Services activities, which are the two programs with a published fee policy, so it is empty across most of the Data Exchange.
value_definition: A whole-dollar number recorded once for the session, appearing in the portal only where the selected program activity and service type make it applicable. The protocols call it a number field in whole dollars only.
limitation: The amount belongs to the session, not to a client, so it cannot be turned into a price per person without assuming the fee was split evenly among everyone who attended, which for family law mediation and group sessions it usually was not. A zero and a blank also read the same way to a reader but mean different things: zero is a session recorded as free, blank is a session where the question was never asked.
rationale: The Data Exchange Protocols define the item twice, once under Commonwealth Home Support Programme fields and once under Family Law Services fields, and give the units and the conditional presentation rule.
evidence_quote: Fees charged: this item is captured at the session level. It allows organisations to report whether the participants of the session were charged a fee to attend the service and reflects the program activity policy regarding fee collection. This item is captured as a dollar figure.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL wording and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without saying the amount is a session total or that the field only exists for two programs.

value_source: DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), section 7.15
variable_description: Whether an interpreter was in the room for this session. The protocols define the field as reporting "whether an interpreter was present for the instance of service to assist with translation and facilitation", and are explicit that it counts either kind: "this could be an interpreter provided by the organisation or someone the client has brought along to help them". It is optional partnership-approach data recorded as yes or no at session level, so it varies within a client's history rather than sitting on the client record.
value_definition: A yes or no flag on the session, one value per session rather than per attendee. It does not name a language and does not distinguish a professional interpreter from a family member acting as one.
limitation: Presence is not need. A session with no interpreter may be one where the client needed one and could not get one, which is the failure most worth finding, and this column cannot separate that case from a session where none was required. Because a family member counts, a high rate of interpreter presence is not evidence of professional interpreting being funded. MAINLANGUAGECODE on the client record is the closest thing to a need measure and it disagrees with this column often.
rationale: The Data Exchange Protocols define the field, state that it is session level and optional, and state that an interpreter brought by the client counts.
evidence_quote: This could be an interpreter provided by the organisation or someone the client has brought along to help them.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL wording and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without saying that an interpreter brought by the client counts or that absence does not mean no need.

value_domain: Money management course label (nine workshops plus other)
value_source: DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), section 6.3.3 and the list of data values
variable_description: Which money management workshop was delivered in this session. The nine are Making Money Last Until Payday, Planning For the Future, How Can Banks Help, Internet and Phone Banking, Credit Can Be a Hazard, Money Loans Sharks and Traps, A Roof Overhead - Home Ownership, A Roof Overhead Tenancy, and Managing Paperwork, with a tenth value for any other workshop. The protocols describe the field as containing "the workshop types able to be delivered under this program activity", allowing organisations "to show that clients have undertaken the required training". It only appears, and is only mandatory, for Commonwealth Financial Counselling and Financial Capability and Money Support Hubs activities when the service type Education and Skills Training is selected.
value_definition: One of ten published labels naming a specific curriculum unit. The numbering runs 1 to 9 in the published order but the workshops are not a sequence a client must work through, so the number carries no progression.
limitation: The value records what was taught in one session, not what a client completed. A client who attended a single workshop and a client who worked through all nine are distinguished only by counting their session rows, and there is no completion or attainment field anywhere in the Data Exchange. Because the field appears under a narrow condition, its absence on a financial counselling session usually means the session was casework rather than that no workshop existed.
rationale: The Data Exchange Protocols define the item under Financial Wellbeing and Capability mandatory fields, state the conditions that make it appear, and publish the ten values.
evidence_quote: Money management course delivered: this item is captured at the session level. The field contains the workshop types able to be delivered under this program activity and allows organisations to show that clients have undertaken the required training.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only that the field indicates 'which of the nine workshop types clients have undertaken' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, when the nine are named in the protocols and the tenth 'other' value is missing from that count.

value_domain: Data Exchange outlet and activity pair identifier
value_source: DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), section 4.5
variable_description: Which funded activity, at which outlet, this session belongs to. The pair exists because the two do not determine each other: the protocols state that "the organisation identifies the program activities each outlet delivers", so one outlet can run several activities and one activity can run from many outlets. That makes this the delivery unit on the ground, and the level at which a question like how many sessions this service ran from this office is actually answerable.
value_definition: A system-generated number, unique to one combination of outlet and program activity. It is an internal Data Exchange key with no external meaning and no structure to decode.
limitation: The pair says nothing about who is funded or who delivers. ORGANISATIONACTIVITYID on the same session row carries the delivery organisation, lead organisation and activity together, and DELIVERYORGID carries the provider, so an outlet operating under a consortium cannot be attributed to a funder from this column alone. The pair is also a configuration record: it exists once an organisation registers an outlet to deliver an activity, whether or not any client was ever seen there.
rationale: The protocols define the outlet, state that program activities are assigned to outlets, and set out the case creation rule that a client receiving the same service from different outlets generates a separate case for each. The pair key itself is described only in the PLIDA data item list, so its behaviour on re-registration is not published.
evidence_quote: The organisation identifies the program activities each outlet delivers.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL wording and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without saying why an outlet and an activity need a joint key or how it differs from the organisation and activity key beside it.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, LeadOrgId in the Attendance (DEX Curated) distribution
variable_description: Which organisation holds the money for the service this record belongs to. DSS describes lead organisations as "organisations that directly receive funding from grants" that "may also deliver the service, or allocate the funding to other Delivery Organisations", so the column is the funding recipient and DELIVERYORGID beside it is the provider. In a single-provider arrangement the two carry the same value; in a consortium they differ, and the difference between them is the only view the Data Exchange gives of subcontracting.
value_definition: A system-generated number of up to nineteen digits, following the same ID number domain as the other Data Exchange organisation and outlet keys. It is an internal key with no structure and no meaning outside the system.
limitation: Counting clients or sessions by lead organisation attributes a whole consortium's caseload to the head body, which for peak organisations and church-based networks can be tens of small services with nothing in common. The identifier also cannot be resolved to a named entity from the data alone: ABN_HASH_TRUNC on the organisation table is the only bridge to anything outside the Data Exchange, and it is a hash rather than a readable ABN.
rationale: The DSS metadata registry publishes the lead organisation and delivery organisation explanations against the same column names in the curated attendance table, and the protocols describe delivery partnership and consortium arrangements at section 4.6.
evidence_quote: Organisations that directly receive funding from grants. These organisations may also deliver the service, or allocate the funding to other Delivery Organisations.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL's parenthetical 'A lead org distributes funding to delivery orgs' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without saying that lead and delivery are equal in most rows and differ only under consortium arrangements.

value_domain: Data Exchange delivery organisation, lead organisation and activity identifier
value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, LeadOrgId and DeliveryOrgId in the Attendance (DEX Curated) distribution
variable_description: The funding arrangement a session or attendance sits under, holding the delivery organisation, the lead organisation and the program activity together in a single number. It exists because none of the three identifies an arrangement on its own: DSS distinguishes "organisations delivering services directly to clients" from "organisations that directly receive funding from grants", and the same provider can deliver the same activity under more than one funder. This is the level at which a grant agreement meets the data.
value_definition: A system-generated number identifying one triple of delivery organisation, lead organisation and activity. It is an internal key with no structure, and it does not contain or reveal the three identifiers it stands for.
limitation: A change of value is not a change of provider. Because three things are folded into one key, a new lead organisation over an unchanged delivery arrangement produces a new identifier, and a provider that keeps delivering the same activity looks discontinuous. Read DELIVERYORGID for the provider, LEADORGID for the funder and ACTIVITYID for the activity, and use this column only to hold an arrangement together.
rationale: The DSS metadata registry publishes the lead and delivery organisation explanations against the same curated attendance table that carries this key, and the PLIDA data item list states that the identifier is the pair of delivery organisation, lead organisation and activity.
evidence_quote: Organisations delivering services directly to clients. These organisations may receive funding directly or through a Funding Recipient (Lead Organisation)
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL wording and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without warning that a compound key changes when any one of its three parts changes.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Data Exchange: Outlet identifier, ID number'; DSS Data Exchange Protocols version 13, section 4.5
variable_description: Which service location a record belongs to, appearing on the outlet table itself and on every table that needs to place a service: attendance, session, client assessment and community assessment. DSS defines it as "a system-generated identifier for a unique outlet record in the Data Exchange, represented by a number", and the protocols define an outlet as "the physical location from where a service is primarily being delivered". It joins to special_outlet, where the outlet's suburb, postcode, state and geocoded boundaries sit.
value_definition: A system-generated number of up to nineteen digits, formatted N[N(18)] in the DSS registry. It is an internal key with no structure and no meaning outside the Data Exchange.
limitation: An outlet is where staff are based, not where the client was seen. The protocols direct organisations to use the nearest administrative premises for mobile services, to use a nearby public place such as a post office or shopping centre for a refuge, and never to create an outlet at a client's home. Distance between an outlet and a client's address is therefore a distance to an office, not to a service. SERVICESETTINGCODE on the session record is what says whether the service happened at the outlet at all.
rationale: The DSS metadata registry publishes the element definition and format, and the protocols publish the outlet definition and the rules that govern which address an outlet may carry.
evidence_quote: A system-generated identifier for a unique outlet record in the Data Exchange, represented by a number.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL wording and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing warned that the outlet address is a staff base rather than the place of service.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Data Exchange: Service provider identifier, ID number'
variable_description: The Data Exchange's own key for a funded organisation, on the organisation table and on every outlet that organisation runs. DSS defines the matching element as "a system-generated identifier for a unique service provider record in the Data Exchange, represented by a number". It is the join that turns a list of outlets into a provider's service network, and it sits beside ABN_HASH_TRUNC on the organisation table, which is the only key that reaches outside the Data Exchange.
value_definition: A system-generated number of up to nineteen digits, formatted N[N(18)] in the DSS registry. It is an internal key with no structure and cannot be resolved to a name, an ABN or an address from the value itself.
limitation: The identifier is a Data Exchange registration, not a legal entity. An organisation that re-registers, merges or changes its funding arrangement can hold more than one, so a count of organisations counts registrations. It also does not say whether the organisation delivered anything: DELIVERYORGID and LEADORGID on the attendance and session records carry the roles, and a registered organisation with no sessions still has a row here.
rationale: The DSS metadata registry publishes the service provider identifier element with the format and definition that the PLIDA data item list echoes for this column. The registry does not publish a separate element for the organisation table's key, so the mapping is read across from the service provider element.
evidence_quote: A system-generated identifier for a unique service provider record in the Data Exchange, represented by a number.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL wording and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without saying what the key joins to or that the ABN beside it is the only external bridge.

value_source: DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026)
variable_description: A second identifier for the same organisation, carried in from the grants system rather than minted by the Data Exchange. It sits on both special_organisation and special_outlet beside ORGANISATIONID, which is the Data Exchange's own key, so the pair is what connects a service reporting performance data to the grant agreement that funds it. The Data Exchange draws activities from DSS grants systems, which SOURCESYSTEMCODE on the activity table records, and this is the organisation half of that provenance.
value_definition: An opaque identifier issued by a DSS grants management system, not by the Data Exchange. Its format is not published and the value carries no readable structure.
limitation: Nothing in the data says what the grants system holds against this identifier, and a reader has no way to resolve it to a grant, a funding amount or an agreement period, because the grants data is not part of PLIDA. It is also not an entity identifier: two organisations under one grant, or one organisation with grants from several programs, need not have a one-to-one relationship with it. ABN_HASH_TRUNC on the organisation table remains the only key that matches a Data Exchange organisation to anything outside DSS.
rationale: The Data Exchange Protocols describe the grant-funded programs the Data Exchange reports on and the organisation and outlet structure the identifier sits in, but DSS publishes no documentation of GovGPS or of this identifier's format, so the reading is inferred from the column name, its placement beside the Data Exchange's own organisation key, and the presence of grants systems in SOURCESYSTEMCODE.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the DIL fragment 'Organisation GovGPS Organisation ID' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the page said nothing beyond restating the variable name.

value_source: DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026)
variable_description: The grants system's identifier for a funded program activity, sitting on the activity table beside the Data Exchange's own ACTIVITYID and PROGRAMID. It is what ties an activity that clients attend to the funding line that pays for it, and it belongs to the same provenance chain as SOURCESYSTEMCODE on the same row, which records whether the activity came from a DSS grants system or from an external one. The activity is the level at which a program becomes something a client can attend from an outlet.
value_definition: An opaque identifier issued by a DSS grants management system, not by the Data Exchange. Its format is not published and the value carries no readable structure.
limitation: The grants system is not in PLIDA, so the identifier cannot be resolved to a grant round, a funding amount or a contract term, and a change of value cannot be told apart from a re-let of the same service. It is also not a program classification: NAME and PROGRAMID on the same row carry the readable program and activity names, and this column will not group activities that a reader would consider the same program.
rationale: The Data Exchange Protocols describe program activities and the grant-funded programs behind them, and the activity table records its source system, but DSS publishes no documentation of GovGPS or of this identifier's format, so the reading is inferred from the column name and its placement beside the Data Exchange's own activity keys.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the DIL fragment 'GPS Program Activity ID' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the page restated the variable name and nothing more.

value_source: DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), section 4.5
variable_description: An indicator carried in from the geocoding of outlet addresses, not a property of the service. Its description in the data item list is not a description at all but the name of the source file, Dex1524outlet_geocoded_addr_a1, the same string that appears against ARID_HASH_TRUNC on the same table, so both columns came out of one address-matching run over Data Exchange outlet addresses for 2015 to 2024. On the evidence of that pairing and of the sibling columns ADDRESSSTATUSCODE, ARID_HASH_TRUNC, MB_ASGS_2021 and SA1_ASGS_2021, it marks how the outlet address resolved rather than anything a client or an organisation reported.
value_definition: A small indicator, most likely binary, produced by the address matching process rather than reported by anyone. Neither the values nor their meanings are published.
limitation: Whatever the flag marks, it describes data processing and not service delivery, so it is never an analysis variable and a difference between outlets on this column is a difference in how their addresses were written down. Because the mapping is not published, a reader cannot tell whether a set flag means a good match or a problem one, and filtering on it risks dropping exactly the outlets whose addresses were hardest to place, which the protocols say include refuges and protected locations.
rationale: The data item list gives the same source file name for this column as for the outlet's address register identifier, which places it in the address geocoding output. No DSS or ABS document describing that output or its flags could be found, so the reading rests on the file name, the column name and the surrounding address columns.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the raw source file name 'Dex1524outlet_geocoded_addr_a1' as its description, guessed a yes-no domain from the variable name, and printed a boilerplate caveat as its limitation.

value_domain: ABS mesh block code, ASGS Edition 3 (2021)
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Main Structure: Mesh Blocks
variable_description: The service outlet's address placed in an ABS mesh block, which is the finest geography on the outlet record. ABS defines mesh blocks as "the smallest geographic areas defined by the ABS" that "form the building blocks for the larger regions of the Australian Statistical Geography Standard", and the SA1, SA2, SA4 and state columns beside it on special_outlet are all aggregations of this one code. It describes where a funded service is based, never where a client lives; the client geography sits on special_client.
value_definition: An eleven-digit code on the 2021 edition of the standard: one digit for state or territory and ten for the mesh block, as in 60106840000 for a Western Australian block. Mesh blocks are redefined at each Census, so a 2021 code has no counterpart in the 2016 columns on the same row.
limitation: A mesh block is a building block, not a place. ABS releases almost nothing at this level beyond dwelling and person counts, so the code is a key for aggregating up or for computing distance, not a unit anything can be described at, and mapping outlets by mesh block produces a picture nobody can read. It is also the outlet's location, so a distance from a client's mesh block measures how far the office is, which the protocols make clear is often not where the service happened.
rationale: The ABS publishes the mesh block definition, the eleven-digit code structure and the role of mesh blocks as the building block of the ASGS main structure. The column sits on the outlet table with the outlet's other geography.
evidence_quote: Mesh Blocks are the smallest geographic areas defined by the ABS and form the building blocks for the larger regions of the Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS).
supersedes_rationale: The entry guessed the domain from the variable name, showed the DIL fragment 'Mesh block coded to 2021 asgs' as its description, and gave a boilerplate limitation about inferred domains rather than saying that the geography belongs to the outlet.

value_domain: Data Exchange SCORE outcome domain label
value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Client outcome assessment: Domain, Label'
variable_description: Which part of a client's life a SCORE rating is about. DSS defines it as "the specific focus of a clients wellbeing measured by a given client outcome assessment, represented by a label", and publishes 24 permissible values that span all four SCORE families at once: circumstance domains such as HOUSING, EMPLOYMENT, MENTAL and MONEY; goal domains such as SKILLS, BEHAVIOURS, KNOWLEDGE and IMPACT; satisfaction; and the community domains including COHESION. Those tokens are the same vocabulary the assistance-needed and referral reference tables use, so a client's presenting reason and their rated outcome can be compared directly.
value_definition: A label of up to seventeen characters, formatted AAA[A(14)], with 24 permissible values plus a supplementary UNKNOWN. The label must be read with OUTCOMETYPE, which says which SCORE family the domain belongs to.
limitation: The set of domains present describes what the service was required or chose to rate, not what mattered to the client. The protocols set a floor and leave the rest to the organisation: providers are "at a minimum, required to report SCOREs for Circumstance domains listed in the Program Specific Guidance", and should "otherwise report a rating against the domain(s) that are most relevant for their client and the outcomes they are aiming to achieve". A domain that is absent was therefore never assessed and cannot be read as a domain in which the client was doing fine, and comparing the domain mix between two organisations compares their programs and their guidance.
rationale: The DSS metadata registry publishes the element definition, its format and the count of permissible values for the same column name in the curated client outcome assessment table, and the protocols publish the domain lists for all four SCORE families.
evidence_quote: The specific focus of a clients wellbeing measured by a given client outcome assessment, represented by a label.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the protocols' guidance paragraph about choosing relevant domains as its description, which reads as advice rather than a definition, and said only that the source defines the value domain.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Client outcome assessment: Domain rating, Five-point scale'; DSS Data Exchange Protocols version 13, section 8.2.2
variable_description: The rating itself, from 1 to 5, for the domain named on the same row. The protocols anchor both ends: 1 means the client's circumstances are "having a significant negative impact on their independence, participation and wellbeing", and 5 means they are "adequate and stable over the medium term" to support it, with 3 as a middle ground between the two negative ratings and the two adequate ones. The scale is the same for all four SCORE families, which is what lets circumstances, goals, satisfaction and community outcomes be reported together.
value_definition: A single digit, 1 to 5, ordinal and with the same direction in every domain: higher is better. The five points are defined by impact on independence, participation and wellbeing rather than by any underlying measurement unit.
limitation: A level is not comparable between clients or between organisations. ASSESSEDBY on the same row records who made the judgement, and the protocols allow the client, the practitioner, both jointly or a support person, using either the SCORE scale directly or a validated instrument translated onto it, so a one-point gap between two rows can be a difference in assessor or in tool. The design use is the change within one client between a paired initial and follow-up rating, not the level.
rationale: The DSS metadata registry publishes the element definition, the five-point value domain and the single-digit format for the same column name in the curated client outcome assessment table, and the protocols define each point of the scale and the assessment methods behind it.
evidence_quote: 1: is used to report that the client's current circumstances are having a significant negative impact on their independence, participation and wellbeing.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL wording 'represented by a score 1-5' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said what the ends of the scale mean or why levels are not comparable.

value_domain: Data Exchange SCORE domain and rating label
value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Client outcome assessment: Domain rating, Label'
variable_description: The domain and the rating fused into one token, such as HOUSING3 or MONEY4. DSS defines it as "an outcome domain rating recorded for a given client outcome assessment, represented by a label" and publishes 60 permissible values of the form domain name followed by a digit. It is worth reaching for over the two columns beside it because each value carries the wording the protocols give that rating in that specific domain, rather than the generic scale, and DSS records that "the permissible values and their meaning are taken from the Data Exchange Protocols".
value_definition: A string of up to eighteen characters, formatted AAA[A(14)]N: a domain label with a trailing digit from 1 to 5. There are 60 values, covering twelve domains at five ratings each.
limitation: It is a string and will not sort, average or difference. Reading it as an ordinal means splitting off the trailing digit, at which point OUTCOMEDOMAINSCORE already holds the number. The 60 values also cover fewer domains than the 24 labels OUTCOMEDOMAIN admits, so this column and the domain column are not interchangeable and a filter written against one will not select the same rows as the same filter written against the other.
rationale: The DSS metadata registry publishes the element definition, the format, the count of permissible values and the note that the values and their meanings come from the Data Exchange Protocols, for the same column name in the curated client outcome assessment table.
evidence_quote: The permissible values and their meaning are taken from the Data Exchange Protocols. The Protocols and its appendices provide context and guidance for organisations reporting outcomes into the Data Exchange.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL wording 'represented by a code' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing revealed that the code is the domain and the rating concatenated.

value_domain: Data Exchange SCORE domain group label
value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Client outcome assessment: Domain group, Label'
variable_description: Which of the four SCORE families a rating belongs to: circumstances, goals, satisfaction or group and community. DSS defines it as "the focus of a clients wellbeing measured by a given client outcome assessment, represented by a label" and publishes exactly those four values. The column appears on both special_client_assessment and special_community_assessment, and the split is clean: the first three occur on the client table and the group value on the community table, because a community SCORE rates a group's capacity rather than a person's circumstances.
value_definition: A label of up to thirteen characters, formatted AAAAA[A(8)], taking one of four values. It groups the domains in OUTCOMEDOMAIN rather than adding information of its own, which is why a domain label is ambiguous without it.
limitation: The type says which family a rating is in, not where it sits in a client's service. Whether a rating is an initial or a follow-up SCORE is carried by ASSESSMENTTYPE, and DSS notes that since 18 August 2018 even that field "is no longer the primary item used to determine assessment order" and should only order assessments made on the same day for the same session. Pairing an initial and follow-up rating therefore needs the assessment dates, not this column.
rationale: The DSS metadata registry publishes the element definition, the format and the four permissible values with their meanings, and the same registry publishes the service phase note on the ordering of assessments.
evidence_quote: The focus of a clients wellbeing measured by a given client outcome assessment, represented by a label.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the DIL's parenthetical listing only the three client-side types and said the source defines the value domain, so a reader had no way to know the fourth value exists on the community assessment table.

value_source: DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols, Version 11, March 2024, section 3.5
variable_description: The suburb of the service outlet, as the funded organisation registered it in the Data Exchange. The protocols define an outlet as "the physical location from where a service is primarily being delivered", so this is where staff are based rather than where a client was seen. It sits with OUTLETPOSTCODE and OUTLETSTATE as the address the organisation typed in, and with ARID_HASH_TRUNC and the ASGS columns as that same address geocoded, which makes it the plain-language label for a row whose other location columns are all codes.
value_definition: Free text holding an Australian locality or suburb name as the organisation entered it, not a code drawn from a classification. There is no validation list behind the field, so spelling, case, abbreviation and the treatment of multi-word names vary between organisations and over time.
limitation: The suburb belongs to the outlet, not to the service delivery. The protocols direct organisations running mobile services to register the nearest administrative premises staff travel from, and to replace a refuge or other protected address with a nearby public place such as a post office or shopping centre, so tallying activity by outlet suburb overstates the suburbs where staff sit and understates the ones where people are helped.
rationale: The protocols define what an outlet is and set the rules that decide which address an organisation may register, which is exactly what governs the content of this field. The registry's own table layout confirms it is one of three free-text address parts on special_outlet.
evidence_quote: For the purposes of the Data Exchange, an outlet is defined as: The physical location from where a service is primarily being delivered.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the domain as an open text domain against a bulk-upload specification, repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, and its description was the custodian's four words, 'Outlet Address: Suburb'.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, value domain 'Australian postcode code', Aristotle item 78
variable_description: The postcode of the premises a funded service is delivered from, one of the three parts of the outlet address the organisation keyed into the Data Exchange. It is the column that supports the comparison the protocols describe between where clients live and where services sit, set against CLIENTPOSTCODE on special_client. Because the value belongs to the outlet's registration, it changes only when the organisation edits the outlet record, not when a service moves.
value_definition: A four-digit Australian postcode. DSS registers the domain as "the Postcode datafile code set representing Australian postcodes as defined by Australia Post", with 0097 reserved for not applicable, 0098 for unknown and 0099 as the default, so the field is a four-character string and leading zeros are meaningful.
limitation: A postcode is a mail delivery area, not a statistical one: postcodes do not nest inside SA2s or local government areas, several can cover one suburb name, and some cover only post office boxes. Anything that has to line up with ABS geography should use the SA and mesh block columns on the same row rather than this field.
rationale: DSS's own metadata registry publishes the postcode value domain used across its collections, including its format, its issuer and its three reserved codes. The protocols separately establish that the outlet address is registered by the organisation.
evidence_quote: The Postcode datafile code set representing Australian postcodes as defined by Australia Post.
supersedes_rationale: The domain was guessed from the variable name, and the value definition and limitation both said only that the domain was inferred and had no finite list.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, value domain 'Australian State or Territory Code', Aristotle item 81
variable_description: The jurisdiction the service outlet sits in, and the coarsest of the three address fields the organisation registered for it. DSS commissions many Data Exchange activities state by state and reports against them the same way, so this is the column that splits a national provider's outlets by administering jurisdiction. STATE_ASGS_2021 on the same row is the same fact derived by ABS from the geocoded address, and is the one to use when the analysis has to join to ABS geography.
value_definition: A state or territory as recorded on the address. DSS registers its state domain as a three-character abbreviation set covering ACT, NSW, NT, QLD, SA, TAS, VIC and WA, with EXT for the other territories and IOB for International Operations Branch, so expect character values rather than the one-digit ABS code carried by the STE boundary columns beside it.
limitation: This is the jurisdiction of the premises, not of the client and not of the funder. A border outlet serves clients from the neighbouring state, and a national program delivered from a single head office reports every one of its sessions against that one state. For a client's own jurisdiction, CLIENTSTATE on special_client is the field.
rationale: DSS's registry publishes the state domain its collections use and gives it as an abbreviation set, and registers the outlet address as a set of physical address elements. The registry's current assignment of the ABS numeric state codeframe to this column is a name-based guess and looks wrong.
evidence_quote: A code set representing Australian states and territories.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the ABS one-digit state codeframe, inferred from the variable name, with the generic sentence about the source defining the domain standing as both definition and limitation.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Client: Participation type, Label', Aristotle item 296
variable_description: Whether the person was at the session as a client or as someone accompanying one. DSS draws the line this way: "A client is a primary recipient of service, and a support person is an individual who is attending the session in order to provide some form of support to the client or clients, but is not receiving that service themselves." Which cohort counts as the client is decided activity by activity, so in Family Law Services the children are the clients and the parents in the room are support persons. On special_client_assessment the same column says whose outcome a SCORE rating belongs to.
value_definition: A short uppercase label. The registry's permissible values are CLIENT for an individual client and SUPPORT for a support person, both in force since 1 July 2014, and the curated Data Exchange attendance table adds GROUP for the rows it writes to stand for unidentified group attendance.
limitation: It records the role the organisation assigned, not whether the person gained anything. Recording support persons is optional, so their absence is no evidence that a client attended alone, and GROUP rows carry no client identifier at all, which means filtering to CLIENT silently discards the aggregate attendance of large groups.
rationale: The DSS metadata registry publishes the data element, its permissible values and a comment that explains the client and support person distinction and how it varies by program activity. The curated attendance distribution documents the extra GROUP value.
evidence_quote: A client is a primary recipient of service, and a support person is an individual who is attending the session in order to provide some form of support to the client or clients, but is not receiving that service themselves.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried three value labels with no explanation, the boilerplate 'The valid_values field contains the source-defined values' as its definition, and the custodian's one-line wording as its description.

value_domain: Personal and family safety outcome domain flag
value_source: DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols, Version 11, March 2024, sections 6.2 and 6.4
variable_description: A flag marking that personal and family safety is one of the domains carried by the key this reference row decodes. The protocols define the domain as "Personal and family safety: where the client is seeking to change the impact of personal and family safety issues on their independence, participation and wellbeing". On special_ref_assistance_needed the column expands a reason-for-assistance key; on special_ref_referral_to it expands a referral purpose key, so the same flag answers two different questions depending on which table it is read from. It is only meaningful after joining the key back to the attendance rows that point at it.
value_definition: One flag column in a wide decode of a reasons key. Its siblings are the other standard domains, AGE, COMMUNITY, EDUCEMPL, EMPLOYMENT, FAMILY, HOUSING, MATERIAL, MENTAL, MONEY, PHYSICAL and TRAINING, with CARING and OTHER added in the referral table, and one key can set several of them at once.
limitation: A set flag records the domain a practitioner chose near the start of service, which the protocols warn is often not the client's real need: they note the real reason is frequently not apparent until after the client engages. Nothing here indicates severity, risk or whether family violence was present, and the whole extended data set is optional, so an unset flag can equally mean the organisation records no reasons at all.
rationale: The protocols publish the eleven standard reason domains and the thirteen referral purposes in the same wording, and the two reference tables in this product carry exactly those domains as columns beside their key.
evidence_quote: Personal and family safety: where the client is seeking to change the impact of personal and family safety issues on their independence, participation and wellbeing.
supersedes_rationale: The domain was 'not specified' and the generic no-value-list sentence stood as both the value definition and the limitation, with the custodian's phrase 'Seeking assistance related to Personal and family safety' as the description.

value_source: DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols, Version 11, March 2024, sections 6.2 and 6.4
variable_description: A flag marking physical health as one of the domains behind the key this reference row decodes. The protocols define it as "Physical health: where the client is seeking to change the impact of their physical health on their independence, participation and wellbeing", which is a statement about participation rather than about a condition. It appears twice in the product with different meanings: on special_ref_assistance_needed it is a reason the client came, and on special_ref_referral_to it is a purpose the client was sent on for.
value_definition: A flag in the wide decode of a reasons key, one of the eleven standardised domains that also form the SCORE circumstance domains. Several flags can be set against a single key, since a client can present with more than one need.
limitation: This is not a health record. It is a service worker's classification of why someone sought help, not a diagnosis, not clinician-reported, and unrelated to the disability, impairment or condition recorded on special_client_disability. A client with a serious physical condition who came for housing help has this flag unset.
rationale: The protocols set out the eleven reason domains and thirteen referral purposes with a definition for each, and the two reference tables carry those domains as flag columns beside their key.
evidence_quote: Physical health: where the client is seeking to change the impact of their physical health on their independence, participation and wellbeing.
supersedes_rationale: The domain was 'not specified' and the generic no-value-list sentence appeared twice, once as the definition and once as the limitation, with no indication that the column belongs to a key decode table.

value_source: DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols, Version 11, March 2024, section 6.2
variable_description: The key identifying the single main reason a client sought help, which the protocols describe as the "Primary reason for seeking assistance: the main reason for seeking assistance, classified as one of eleven possible categories". Join it to special_ref_assistance_needed to turn it into the named domain flags. ASSISTANCENEEDEDKEY sits beside it on the same attendance row and holds the secondary reasons, which the protocols expect to be one or two more.
value_definition: An integer key into the special_ref_assistance_needed reference table rather than a code that can be read on its own. The reference row it points at sets exactly one of the eleven standard reason columns for this field, since only one primary reason is allowed.
limitation: The reason belongs to the case, not to the session, so it repeats unchanged across every attendance row for that case and cannot show how a client's presenting need moved over a course of service. It is also optional partnership-approach data, so it is systematically absent for organisations that report only the priority requirements, and absence is not 'no reason given'.
rationale: The protocols define the primary reason for seeking assistance, state that it is recorded at case level and list the eleven categories. The reference table in this product carries those eleven categories as columns keyed by the value this column holds.
evidence_quote: Primary reason for seeking assistance: the main reason for seeking assistance, classified as one of eleven possible categories.
supersedes_rationale: The domain was 'not specified', the generic no-value-list sentence stood as both definition and limitation, and nothing said the value was a key into another table.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Data Exchange: Program identifier, ID number', Aristotle item 1396
variable_description: The funding program a program activity belongs to, defined by DSS as "an identifier for a unique program record in the Data Exchange, represented by a number". On special_program it is the key of the program lookup, paired with NAME; on special_activity it says which program each activity rolls up to, which makes it the column that reduces a long list of activities to the handful of budget programs reported against. The published values run from 20, Programme 2.1 Families and Communities, to 30, Program 2.4 Refugee and Humanitarian Assistance, and include state agencies such as the NSW Department of Communities and Justice as well as NDIA and aged care lines.
value_definition: A two-digit number from a short published list. Each value carries a start date, the earliest being 4 September 2015, and one value has closed: 24, NSW Family and Community Services, ended on 1 August 2019 and was replaced by 25, NSW Department of Communities and Justice.
limitation: The program is a funding line, not a service. Two activities under one program can be quite different kinds of help, and a client counted under a program has not necessarily received anything its title suggests. Because programs are renamed and renumbered when agencies restructure, a series that spans one of those changes will break unless the old and new values are combined by hand.
rationale: The DSS metadata registry publishes the program identifier data element with its full permissible value list, its two-digit format and the start and end dates of each value, which is precisely the domain this column carries.
evidence_quote: An identifier for a unique program record in the Data Exchange, represented by a number.
supersedes_rationale: The domain was 'not specified' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice over, and the description was the custodian's 45-word abstract definition of the word 'program' rather than anything about the Data Exchange.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, Client (DEX Curated) distribution, which lists the column beside CurrentRecord, SysStartTime and SysEndTime without publishing its definition
variable_description: The position of this row in the version history of the record it describes. The seven reference tables that carry it — activity, client, client disability, organisation, outlet, program and service type — are delivered as full histories rather than snapshots, so one outlet or one client appears once per version and this column orders those versions. CURRENTRECORD flags which version is live and SYSSTARTTIME and SYSENDTIME give the window each was in force; count without filtering on one of them and a single outlet becomes several.
value_definition: A positive integer counting upwards within one entity's history, so it is unique only in combination with that entity's identifier and is never a key on its own.
limitation: A new sequence number means a field on the record changed, not that anything happened to the client or the service: a corrected postcode and a genuine relocation both produce one. The column also does not say which field changed, so any change history has to be rebuilt by comparing consecutive versions.
rationale: The DSS curated client distribution lists RecordSeqNbr in the same block as CurrentRecord, SysStartTime and SysEndTime, and the registry shows the seven DEX tables that carry it are exactly the reference tables that also carry those versioning columns. The custodian's own wording, 'sequence of historical records', agrees, but no published page defines the values, so this stays guessed.
supersedes_rationale: The domain was 'not specified', the generic no-value-list sentence stood as both definition and limitation, and the description was the custodian's own eight words.
description_source: Inferred from the variable name, its table and the custodian's own wording

value_source: DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols, Version 11, March 2024, section 6.3
variable_description: Who sent the client to this organisation. The protocols put it plainly: "Referral source is the person or agency responsible for referring a client to an organisation." The categories follow AIHW collection definitions and fall into agency sources such as health, community services, education, legal, employment, Centrelink, My Aged Care, NDIS and Local Area Coordinator referrals, non-agency sources such as self, family, friends and a general practitioner, and a not stated category. It answers how people reach a service, which the outward referral columns on the same row cannot.
value_definition: A label from a fixed list of about twenty categories grouped under agency, non-agency and not stated. The agency group is the long one, running from health, community services, educational and legal agencies through to 'Lender/financial agency', 'Accounting agency', Centrelink, My Aged Care Gateway and the NDIS and Local Area Coordinator referral categories.
limitation: The source is recorded once per case, so a client who returns through a different pathway keeps the value from the first time, and a case that ran for years still shows how it began. 'Self' also covers two different things, a genuine self-referral and a client who could not say who suggested the service, and the field is optional, so blank means unrecorded far more often than unknown.
rationale: The protocols define referral source, state that it is recorded at case level, explain that the classification comes from AIHW data collection definitions and publish the category list.
evidence_quote: Referral source is the person or agency responsible for referring a client to an organisation.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried source-defined values with the boilerplate 'The valid_values field contains the source-defined values' as its definition and 'The source defines the value domain' as its limitation, saying nothing about case-level recording.

value_source: DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols, Version 11, March 2024, section 6.4
variable_description: The date a referral out to a different organisation was recorded against this session. It pairs with REFERRALTOEXTERNALKEY, which says what the referral was for, and mirrors REFERRALTOINTERNALDATE for referrals kept inside the same provider. Because the protocols allow only one external referral per session record, a client sent to two outside services on one day has to appear as two sessions, so this date can be repeated across sessions that describe a single conversation.
value_definition: A calendar date at day resolution. Data Exchange dates are entered as dd/mm/yyyy and the registry's session dates are registered in DDMMYYYY form, so there is no time component to work with.
limitation: It records that a referral was made, not that the client ever arrived: nothing in the Data Exchange links this row to a later record at the receiving organisation, so referral counts cannot be turned into service take-up. Since the referral is captured on the session record, the date normally sits on the session itself and is not an independent event date.
rationale: The protocols establish that referrals out are recorded at the session level, one internal and one external per session, and that any further referrals have to be split into separate sessions, which is what governs how the dates on this column behave.
evidence_quote: Referrals are recorded at the session level and can include one internal and one external type of referral per session record.
supersedes_rationale: The domain was 'not specified' and the generic no-value-list sentence was printed twice, as the value definition and again as the limitation.

value_source: DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols, Version 11, March 2024, section 6.4
variable_description: The key describing why a client was referred out of this organisation at this session. The protocols define the external type as a referral "made to a service that is provided by a different organisation", as against the internal type carried by REFERRALTOINTERNALKEY. Join the value to special_ref_referral_to to expand it into the thirteen referral purpose flags, which are the eleven SCORE outcome domains plus support to a caring role and other.
value_definition: An integer key into the special_ref_referral_to lookup rather than a purpose code in its own right. The row it points at can set more than one purpose flag, so one key can carry several reasons for the referral.
limitation: One external referral is permitted per session, so the column undercounts a session in which several outside referrals were made unless the organisation split them across sessions. It names a purpose and never a destination, so it cannot be used to map which agencies receive referrals or to check whether the receiving service exists.
rationale: The protocols define the internal and external referral types, publish the thirteen referral purposes, and state the one-per-session rule. The reference table in this product carries exactly those purposes as columns keyed by this value.
evidence_quote: External: made to a service that is provided by a different organisation
supersedes_rationale: The domain was 'not specified' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, and nothing indicated the value was a key into a purpose lookup.

value_source: DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols, Version 11, March 2024, section 6.4
variable_description: The date a client was referred to another service inside the same organisation at this session. With REFERRALTOINTERNALKEY it forms half of the client pathways data the protocols place at session level, the other half being the external referral columns on the same row. Both are extended partnership-approach items, so the column is populated only for organisations that agreed to collect the extended data set.
value_definition: A calendar date at day resolution, entered as dd/mm/yyyy in the Data Exchange, with no time component.
limitation: An internal referral moves a client between services within one provider, so it produces no new organisation anywhere in the data and cannot be traced to an outcome. A provider that runs a single funded activity has nowhere to refer internally, so a low rate of internal referral dates reflects how many services a provider operates as much as how often it refers.
rationale: The protocols set out that referrals out are session-level items, define the internal type, and cap them at one of each type per session, which is what shapes this date column.
evidence_quote: Data is recorded about referrals made to other services to reflect a client's need for help outside the scope of the funded activity.
supersedes_rationale: The domain was 'not specified', and the value definition and limitation were the same generic sentence about no finite value list.

value_source: DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols, Version 11, March 2024, section 6.4
variable_description: The key describing why a client was moved to another service within the same organisation at this session. The protocols define this type as a referral "made to another service offered within the same organisation", which is the whole difference between this column and REFERRALTOEXTERNALKEY. Both resolve through the same lookup, special_ref_referral_to, so the purpose vocabulary is shared and only the direction differs.
value_definition: An integer key into the special_ref_referral_to lookup. The row it resolves to sets one or more of the thirteen referral purpose flags, so a single key value can stand for several purposes at once.
limitation: It cannot tell you which internal service received the client, only what the referral was for, and there is no link to the case or session the client turned up in next. Because both key columns point at the same lookup, reading the purpose without also checking which column it came from loses the internal against external distinction that is the point of the pair.

For any question about outreach models or about the shift to remote delivery, this is the column that holds the answer.

The registry's permissible values, in force from 18 August 2018, are ORGOUTLETOFFICE, CLRES, COMMVENUE, PARORG, TELE, DIGITAL, HEALTHFACILITY, EDUFACILITY and JUSTICEFACILITY; the March 2024 protocols describe Telephone, Video and Online service as three separate settings where the registry carries the single DIGITAL value beside TELE.

evidence_quote: The date a given client outcome assessment was entered into a system, represented by DDMMYYYY.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Data Exchange: Session identifier, ID number', Aristotle item 1775
